title: Initiative Measure 440: Authorize Laws Allowing Online Sports Wagering

context.text: Initiative Measure 440 is a citizen initiative. Nebraska Secretary of State Bob Evnen certified it for the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot on Sept. 11, 2026, and the number was assigned at random from 440-442. The Examiner reported that signature fraud allegations affected all four statewide ballot-measure petitions, that six out-of-state circulators had been arrested in a criminal investigation, and that one other initiative (from Respect Nebraska Voters) was removed from the ballot by the Nebraska Supreme Court. A companion statute is on the ballot as Initiative Measure 441.

question.text: Shall the Nebraska Constitution be amended to authorize the enactment of laws allowing persons located within Nebraska to place sports wagers through an Internet-based platform when offered by an authorized gaming operator conducting games of chance within a licensed racetrack enclosure in Nebraska?

summary.text: Initiative 440 would amend Article III, section 24 of the Nebraska Constitution to add a subsection stating that the section's limits on games of chance do not apply to laws licensing, authorizing, regulating or taxing games of chance conducted by authorized gaming operators within a licensed racetrack enclosure, including sports wagering over the Internet if the person placing the wager is located in Nebraska when the wager is placed. The constitutional amendment itself does not set the rules; it allows the Legislature to enact them.

measure.yesMeans: A vote FOR will amend the Nebraska Constitution to authorize the enactment of laws to allow persons located within Nebraska to place sports wagers through an Internet-based platform when offered by an authorized gaming operator conducting games of chance within a licensed racetrack enclosure in Nebraska.
measure.noMeans: A vote AGAINST means the Nebraska Constitution will not be amended in this manner.

argumentsFor.text: Official pamphlet, supporters contend: “Vote FOR Initiative 440 to legalize online sports wagering and direct more than $166 million to property tax relief.”

Official pamphlet, supporters contend: “Initiative 440 keeps the money in Nebraska through a legal, regulated and secure marketplace that is projected to deliver more than $166 million in direct property tax relief to Nebraska homeowners, farmers, ranchers and small businesses over the next ten years.”

argumentsAgainst.text: Official pamphlet, opponents contend: “Initiative Measure 440 turns every phone into a casino, every play into a wager, and every athlete into a target—sending hundreds of millions of dollars out of Nebraska to out-of-state gambling conglomerates.”

Official pamphlet, opponents contend: “Every teenager with a phone will face aggressive advertising, while taxpayers and families get no real property tax relief, as casinos promised five years ago, and will be forced to pay for increased social costs.”

sources.title: Informational Pamphlet on Initiative Measures Appearing on the 2026 General Election Ballot
Secretary of State Evnen certifies Nebraska’s fall 2026 ballot after lawsuit-heavy summer

researchNotes: Arguments are the 'Supporters contend' and 'Opponents contend' statements printed in the Secretary of State's official pamphlet, which says they are 'derived from information provided to the Secretary of State from supporters and opponents'; the pamphlet does not name the authors. The revenue figures in the arguments are the arguments' own claims, not an official fiscal estimate. The pamphlet summarises each side in one paragraph, so the two items per side are separate sentences from the same paragraph, not combined.
